options.text: Neither document mentions it, so it is left to the laboratory's discretion.
options.why: Both address it, in different directions.

items.explanation: RPL (losses after a confirmed pregnancy) and RIF (no positive test after transfers) are not interchangeable.

items.stem: On PGT-A, which set of positions of the ESHRE RIF document (2023), the ESHRE add-ons document (2023) and NICE NG257 is correct?

options.text: RIF: considers it; add-ons: “currently not recommended for routine clinical use”; NICE: do not offer it for live birth.
options.why: Correct: this is one of the disagreements between documents (NICE 1.48.1).

options.text: RIF: “not recommended”; add-ons: “recommended” in advanced maternal age; NICE: offer it after two failed transfers.
options.why: All three positions are altered.

options.text: RIF: explicitly recommends it; add-ons: “not recommended”; NICE: does not address PGT-A.
options.why: The RIF document only considers it, the add-ons phrase is a different one and NICE does address it (1.48.1).

options.text: All three documents agree on “not recommended”, with no nuance or exceptions between them.
options.why: They disagree: the RIF document considers it.

items.explanation: On immunotherapy they agree not to use it; on PGT-A, the RIF document is the most open.

items.stem: How do the ESHRE RPL guideline (2022) and the ESHRE RIF document (2023) differ on antiphospholipids and thyroid?

options.text: Both strongly recommend them in all patients, with no differences between the two populations.
options.why: In RIF, thyroid testing can only be considered and antiphospholipids depend on risk factors.

options.text: In RPL, only to be considered; in RIF, both strongly recommended after two failed transfers.
options.why: It is the other way round: recommended (strong) in RPL and more limited in RIF.

options.text: RPL: both recommended (strong); RIF: antiphospholipids if at risk (to consider otherwise) and thyroid to consider.
options.why: Correct: the same test can carry different weight depending on the population.

options.text: Neither document addresses thyroid: both refer directly to thyroid guidelines.
options.why: Both address it: recommended in RPL and to be considered in RIF.

items.explanation: Before applying a recommendation, check which population it refers to.

items.stem: A couple with RIF (fictional case) asks whether “it makes sense to continue”. What prognostic figure does the ESHRE RIF document report?

options.text: That fewer than 5% of patients with RIF achieve a live birth, so moving to donation is advisable.
options.why: Invented figure that contradicts the cited study.

options.text: That all patients with RIF achieve a live birth if treated with immunotherapy.
options.why: Invented claim; immunotherapy is not recommended in RIF.

options.text: That prognosis cannot be estimated, because every RIF case is different and there are no studies.
options.why: The document cites a study and proposes using the individual implantation estimate.

options.text: That, according to a cited study, half of patients with RIF achieve a live birth with ART within 5 years.
options.why: Correct: it supports data-based hope, together with the individual estimate for the next cycle.

items.explanation: The couple can be reassured with their individual estimate of implantation in the next cycle.

items.stem: Which approach to support in RIF does the ESHRE document describe?

options.text: Honesty about the evidence, or its absence, and the suggestion of planning several cycles allowing for failure.
options.why: Correct: it adapts the supportive care elements of the RPL guideline.

options.text: Always offer some additional test or treatment, because the couple needs to feel that action is taken.
options.why: The document warns that many interventions are applied empirically under pressure to act.

options.text: Avoid discussing probabilities, because figures increase stress in patients with RIF.
options.why: The document proposes using the individual implantation estimate to reassure.

options.text: Focus on the man, because in RIF he reports more stress and social isolation than the woman herself.
options.why: The data refer to women; there are no data on men.

items.explanation: Women with RIF report more stress than fertile controls, social isolation and less hope after repeated cycles.

acog-2018-pb197-thrombophilia.title: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 197: Inherited Thrombophilias in Pregnancy
acog-2018-pb197-thrombophilia.authors: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists' Committee on Practice Bulletins—Obstetrics
acog-2018-pb197-thrombophilia.population: Pregnant women and women considered for inherited thrombophilia evaluation.
acog-2018-pb197-thrombophilia.finding: Because of the lack of association between heterozygosity or homozygosity for MTHFR C677T and adverse pregnancy outcomes (including VTE), screening with MTHFR mutation analyses or fasting homocysteine is not recommended (Level B). MTHFR mutations by themselves do not appear to increase VTE risk.
acog-2018-pb197-thrombophilia.limitations: Full text read (Obstet Gynecol 2018;132:e18–34) from an academic copy of the published PDF. Whether ACOG has reaffirmed or replaced it after 2018 was not verified. US context.

eshre-2022-rpl.title: ESHRE guideline: recurrent pregnancy loss: an update in 2022
eshre-2022-rpl.authors: ESHRE Guideline Group on RPL; Bender Atik R, Christiansen OB, Elson J, et al.
eshre-2022-rpl.population: Couples with recurrent pregnancy loss (two or more losses).
eshre-2022-rpl.finding: Low-dose folic acid has not been shown to prevent loss in unexplained RPL (strong); do not use high doses without hyperhomocysteinaemia or conditions raising NTD risk (diabetes, epilepsy). Prophylactic vitamin D may be considered in preconception counselling (GPP) although evidence of effectiveness is absent; vitamin D testing to find a cause is not recommended. Multivitamins: advise options safe in pregnancy (GPP); they are not a treatment. Sperm DNA fragmentation in couples with RPL: could be considered for diagnostic purposes, using a validated test (conditional; ⊕⊕⊕○). Parental karyotyping: not routine; can be carried out after an individual risk assessment (conditional).
eshre-2022-rpl.limitations: Recommendations table and vitamin D chapter read in the full ESHRE PDF. Specific RPL population; several recommendations are good practice points (GPP), not trial-based. Recommendations on sperm DNA fragmentation and parental karyotyping checked in the HRO summary (hoad002) and in the justification of the full PDF.

eshre-2023-addons.title: Good practice recommendations on add-ons in reproductive medicine
eshre-2023-addons.authors: ESHRE Add-ons Working Group; Lundin K, Bentzen JG, Bozdag G, Ebner T, Harper J, Le Clef N, Moffett A, Norcross S, Polyzos NP, Rautakallio-Hokkanen S, Sfontouris I, Sermon K, Vermeulen N, Pinborg A
eshre-2023-addons.population: Patients undergoing assisted reproductive technology (ART); Hum Reprod 2023 (ESHRE Pages).
eshre-2023-addons.finding: 42 recommendations using its own four-phrase scale (recommended; can be considered; currently not recommended for routine clinical use; not recommended). Peripheral blood immune tests and uterine NK-cell testing: not recommended. Screening hysteroscopy: currently not recommended for routine clinical use (can be considered in recurrent implantation failure). Sperm DNA damage testing, endometrial scratching and KIR/HLA genotyping: currently not recommended for routine clinical use. ICSI for non-male factor infertility: not recommended.
eshre-2023-addons.limitations: Full text read (UCL Discovery open-access copy of the advance online version); the wording of every cited recommendation and the scale-definition table were checked verbatim. Good practice recommendations based on review and consensus, not a GRADE guideline: no recommendation rests on high-quality evidence and only four on moderate-quality evidence. ART population, not specifically unexplained infertility.

eshre-2023-rif.title: ESHRE good practice recommendations on recurrent implantation failure
eshre-2023-rif.authors: ESHRE Working Group on Recurrent Implantation Failure; Cimadomo D, de los Santos MJ, Griesinger G, Lainas G, Le Clef N, McLernon DJ, Montjean D, Toth B, Vermeulen N, Macklon N
eshre-2023-rif.population: Patients and couples undergoing IVF/ICSI with recurrent implantation failure; Hum Reprod Open 2023 (ESHRE Pages). Assumes a standard fertility work-up completed before ART.
eshre-2023-rif.finding: Defines RIF individually with a 60% threshold of cumulative predicted chance of implantation. 19 recommendations on investigations and 13 on interventions, classed as recommended, to be considered or not recommended. Recommended: review lifestyle, re-assess endometrial thickness, genetic counselling if a chromosomal abnormality is found, antiphospholipid antibodies with risk factors. To be considered: karyotyping, hysteroscopy, chronic endometritis, thyroid, PGT-A, blastocyst transfer. Not recommended: NK cells, cytokines, HLA-C, microbiome, sperm DNA fragmentation, scratching, G-CSF, intralipid, IVIG, PBMC, PRP, intrauterine hCG, heparin, GnRHa/AI pre-treatment, assisted hatching.
eshre-2023-rif.limitations: Full text read in the Europe PMC open-access XML version (PMC10270320); the PDF could not be downloaded and the colour-coded summary figures (images) were not read, only the table wording. Good practice document based on expert opinion supported by the literature and a survey, without GRADE ratings; RIF definitions vary across studies.

nice-2026-ng257.title: Fertility problems: assessment and treatment (NG257)
nice-2026-ng257.authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
nice-2026-ng257.population: People with fertility problems in the UK health system.
nice-2026-ng257.finding: Do not use AMH to predict clinical pregnancy through spontaneous conception (1.18.3). Use AMH or AFC as predictors of ovarian response to inform decisions and counselling about the likelihood of live birth after assisted conception (1.18.4). Do not use FSH as a predictor (1.18.5). Refer at presentation if the woman is 36 or over or there is a known cause or predisposing factors (1.16.8); otherwise investigation after 1 year of unprotected intercourse. Unexplained fertility problems: keep trying for 2 years in total before treatment (1.38.1); do not offer ovarian stimulation as a stand-alone treatment (1.38.2); then consider up to 4 cycles of IUI with gonadotrophins or offer IVF (1.38.3). Male factor: repeat an abnormal semen analysis, ideally at 3 months (1.17.4); do not test sperm DNA fragmentation (1.17.6); do not offer androgens (1.24.3). Endometriosis: expectant management for up to 2 years (including time already spent trying) or surgery; then consider up to 4 cycles of IUI with gonadotrophins or offer IVF (1.36.1–1.36.3). Add-ons: do not offer endometrial scratch or hysteroscopy as pre-treatment (1.40.1–1.40.2), endometrial receptivity testing (1.41.1), immunological agents (1.42.1) or PGT-A (1.48.1); do not offer assisted hatching (1.49.1, from 2004); ICSI: offer with surgically retrieved sperm or frozen–thawed oocytes, consider with abnormal semen or previous failed fertilisation, and do not use without male factor (1.50.1–1.50.5).
nice-2026-ng257.limitations: NHS (UK) context; replaces CG156. Numbering checked in the March 2026 PDF.
